eligibility_note: Own IV-GMM panel estimation, 79 economies (Appendix Table 1), 1990-2018; exposures are broadband, internet, mobile and fixed telephone (ICT goods imports and transport are extra exposures); outcomes are HDI, human capital, life expectancy, child and maternal mortality (living standards beyond income). Meets all criteria.

sample_corrections.sample.economies_or_groups: South Asia 7, sub-Saharan Africa 45 (not 'about 44'), Latin America-Caribbean 27, total 79 (counted from Appendix Table 1 list, p.22)
sample_corrections.results[8] N: Table 2E N for the ICT columns (5-9) is 148, 175, 150, 173, 172, i.e. 148-175, not 120-175; 54 and 120 are the rail and port-connectivity columns
sample_corrections.exposure_measure locator: Indicators are entered one at a time in Tables 2A-2E (cols 5-9), not 'Table 1' (Table 1 only defines variables)

results.correction: Values match Table 2C cols 5-9 (0.012***, 0.026***, -0.012**, 0.011***, 0.011***); SEs 0.001-0.006 correct. Direction 'positive' hides the negative ICT-goods coefficient, which the record does list.

Values match Table 2D cols 5-9. The 'positive' direction label means beneficial (fewer deaths); the coefficients themselves are negative for broadband, telephone, internet and mobile and positive (+0.519) for ICT goods. Dependent variable is the number of under-five deaths (Table 1), so it is a count, not a rate.

Coefficients and SEs are right (broadband -0.070** (0.028), telephone -0.278*** (0.089), internet -0.077** (0.036), mobile -0.033 (0.033), ICT goods 0.085 (0.095)). Sample size is wrong: N for these columns is 148, 175, 150, 173, 172 (148-175), not 120-175.

heterogeneity.correction: Text confirms positive broadband/telephone/internet/mobile slopes on HDI in all three regions, negative ICT-goods slope in SAR and LAC and positive in SSA, and negative maternal-mortality slopes for broadband, internet and mobile in SAR and LAC with positive in SSA. Interaction estimates are indeed only in the supplementary material (plots in Figs 1B-1J), so no coefficients or SEs can be checked.
heterogeneity.quote: The broadband penetration slope is positive for all the regions  [Sec 4.2.1, p.12]

heterogeneity.correction: No income-group analysis exists; only SSA and LAC dummies versus SAR. SSA dummy on HDI ranges -0.119 to -0.228 in Table 2A, so 'about -0.12 to -0.23' is right.
heterogeneity.quote: The regional dummies indicate that relative to SAR countries  [p.11]

income_group_note: Paper reports no income-group results; the record's 'not reported' entries are correct. Sample is regional (SAR, SSA, LAC) and mixes low to high-income economies (e.g. Bahamas, Barbados, Chile, Uruguay, Seychelles).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - causal wording ('impact', 'improve', IV-GMM said to address reverse causality) but the instrument is never named, Hansen J is 0.000 in Tables 2B-2D, and the notes say 'a single instrument' while listing 11 instruments.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - WDI penetration rates in logs are standard but values near zero give extreme minima (-10.953 for internet), and ICT-goods imports is a weak adoption proxy.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree - unbalanced panel chosen 'strictly based on data availability', N from 54 to 785, only three developing regions.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - HDI contains an income component while GDP per capita is a control, maternal mortality is modelled, and under-five mortality is a count of deaths (Table 1).
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - serious is justified because F-statistics are identical across Tables 2B, 2C and 2D (132664.515, 68711.829, ...) and are implausibly large, with no first stage or instrument described.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - moderate is defensible because regional interaction results are only in supplementary plots, although the record's own example of a text-table mismatch is garbled and not an actual mismatch (text and tables agree).
risk_of_bias.why: Serious fits: causal claims rest on an unidentified instrument and copy-paste first-stage diagnostics; borderline critical for the mortality tables, but the OLS-like correlations are still informative.

problems: No invented or mixed-up results. Errors: SSA count given as 'about 44' (45 in Appendix Table 1); LAC 'about 27' is exactly 27; maternal-mortality N range 120-175 should be 148-175 (record's RoB says 54-175 for all maternal models, which only holds across all nine columns); exposure-measure locator should be Tables 2A-2E. The selective_reporting rationale contains a self-contradictory sentence. Also note direction coding for under-five deaths follows 'beneficial' not coefficient sign.

Meets all criteria.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - level regressions on persistent ICT stocks with initial-stock lag and G2SLS using own lags (t-2 to t-4) as instruments, no overidentification or weak-instrument tests, and footnote 18 admits 'risk to be affected by endogeneity' while the introduction claims results are 'not affected by endogeneity'.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - counts of lines, hosts, phones and PCs per capita ignore quality (footnote 14), the composite is an unweighted average of normalised proxies, and hosts have many zeros.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree - samples driven by data availability (88 to 99 countries, only 47 for mobile and PCs), short 1991-97 window, and series starting after 1985 for many countries.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - GDP per working-age person at PPP from WDI is a standard output measure.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - many robustness results (alternative labour input, trend income, Levine-Renelt variables, freedom indices, MRW restriction removed) are only 'available upon request'.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - abstract overstates (hosts never estimated alone; g_ICT insignificant for phone lines and 1991-97 composite in Table 3), text '.02/.12' loose versus Table 2, identical R2 0.9127 for phone and composite columns in Table 1, and a truncated conclusion sentence.
risk_of_bias.why: Causal language ('effect', 'role', 'not affected by endogeneity') with only lagged-own-variable instruments and a small cross-section is serious, not moderate.

problems: Record is largely accurate. Corrections: phone-line column has 88 economies (not within 94-99); human-capital significance claim for mobile phones overstated (still 10% significant). Additional inconsistencies in the paper not in the record: text gives implied beta .23 while Table 1 shows 0.242; Table 3 labels initial stock as 1985 for 1991-97 columns while footnote 18 says A_ICT(0) is the first sample year (cannot be checked).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - predetermined US-based exposure scores limit reverse causation but only sector and country dummies are used and AI exposure is strongly tied to education (Felten percentile 26.6 low-educ vs 75.1 high-educ, Table A1), so skill-biased demand shifts are not separated; moderate is the right level.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - potential-exposure indices crosswalked from US SOC, only moderately correlated across AI measures (rs = 0.64), and Webb AI coefficient rises from 0.104 to 0.192 when software exposure is added (Table B1 col 4).
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree - 16 countries with EU-LFS wage deciles, start fixed by the 2011 ISCO break, some wage reference years substituted (AT, ES, LT 2018; FI 2017; UK 2013 start).
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - employment-share change from LFS cells is fine; wages come from deciles converted to cell centiles, which is coarse.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - simple main specification but clustering is inconsistent (text 'sector-clustered', table notes 'clustered by country' with 16 clusters) and many subgroup and country regressions are run.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - software null, wage nulls, negative countries and unsupported routinisation are reported, with country tables in Appendix B; low is fair.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard descriptive-association design with predetermined exposure, no causal strategy beyond that, and cautious wording in most places; moderate is appropriate.

problems: No invented numbers or mixed-up papers found; all six pooled results and the Table 5 correlations match. Minor: 'about double' overstatement for age pattern; Table B1 notes list column 3 as Software and column 4 as Robots while the rows show Robot in col 3 and Software in col 4 (record's reading of the rows is correct); text says weights are average employment, table notes say average labour supply. The authors also use 'impact' wording in places (conclusion: 'positive impact of AI-enabled automation on employment holds across countries') despite stating the results are statistical associations.

income_group_note: No income grouping; EU27 only, as the record says.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - moderate fits (2SRI with lags, difference and two-step GMM, Granger test in the supplement) but the record's evidence is muddled: Table C1's r = 0.1385 (p = 0.0007) is for the differenced lag dLog(ICT) in t-1, which is not the instrument used; the instruments in Table C2 are Log(ICT) in t-1 and t-2, which Table C1 shows uncorrelated with employment growth (0.0022, -0.0032). Still, the first-stage coefficients 0.458 and -0.494 nearly offset, so the instrument pair behaves like lagged growth, which makes the exclusion restriction questionable (my inference from Table C2).
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - PIM stock from Eurostat GFCF by asset with uniform 33% depreciation from Corrado et al. and linear interpolation of missing values.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree - all EU27 members and 1995-2019 with no evident selection, but the 22 observations per country are unexplained.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - total employment in thousand persons from Eurostat national accounts, persons not hours.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - many alternatives (27 country interactions, median splits, sub-periods, GDP weights), and country regressions switch between OLS and 2SRI depending on the significance of rho.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - SEs for country, group and sub-period results are only in the online supplement (Tables S4-S8); pooled results with SEs are positive for all estimators.
risk_of_bias.why: Reasonable short-run differenced panel with an explicit endogeneity strategy whose instruments are lags of the regressor; exogeneity not established, so moderate.

problems: No invented or mixed-up numbers; all reported coefficients, SEs and job counts match the tables. One misreading in the record: Table C1 does not show that the instruments used are correlated with employment growth; it shows the differenced lag is, while the log-level lags used in Table C2 are 'Uncorrelated'. The authors' claim that instruments 'are valid' rests on Table C2 first-stage fit and an error-term correlation of 0.0074 (p = 0.8564), which is weak evidence. Note also the footnote-8 statement that Granger causality is unidirectional is not shown in the paper (online Table S1).
